title: Retry & Backoff Policy Spec + SDK Compatibility Matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: We have divergent retry/timeout/backoff behaviors across services and client SDKs that undermine SLOs and complicate multi-region failover and incident response. Some clients retry aggressively without idempotency keys; others rely on hedged requests inconsistently. This ticket defines a cross-service runtime + SDK contract for safe retries, standardized timeouts/backoffs, idempotency key rules, hedged request guardrails, circuit breaker signals, and load-shedding behavior. Goals: 1) prevent duplicate side-effects when clients retry; 2) ensure predictable latency/cost trade-offs for hosted and dedicated customers; 3) provide a migration path for older SDKs without breaking production; 4) enable multi-region failover with coordinated retry/backoff to avoid synchronized storms.
acceptance_criteria: SDK compatibility matrix published and reviewed by SDK owners
Runtime implements server-side idempotency token handling for retryable endpoints with a 24h dedup window and configurable storage backend
SDKs (python/js/go) implement the default policy flags and unit + integration tests
Canary traffic rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) behind feature flag with rollback plan
Monitoring: dashboards for client retry rates, idempotency conflicts, hedged request ratio, circuit-breaker state, and P95/P99 tail latencies
Runbook updated with failure modes and escalation steps
No regressions on core SLOs in canary (availability >= 99.9%, P95 latency within 10% of baseline)
spec_summary: Core proposal (high level): Default client retry policy: up to 2 retries for idempotent-safe operations (total attempts = 3), exponential backoff with base 100ms, multiplier 2, full jitter, max_backoff 3000ms, and an overall client-side deadline of 8s. For non-idempotent endpoints, retries are allowed only when an Idempotency-Key header is supplied (UUIDv4 recommended) and server advertises idempotency support. Server deduplication TTL default = 24 hours. Hedged requests are opt-in per endpoint: allow a single hedged duplicate when observed tail latency exceeds configured P95 threshold for that model/route; hedged attempts must be limited per-client and globally rate-limited to avoid amplification. Circuit breaker signals: open when 5xx rate > 5% or error rate increases by >x2 over baseline in a 1-minute sliding window, with exponential cooldown and progressive reopen checks. Load-shedding: runtime should reject the lowest-priority requests first with 429 + Retry-After and provide a clear Failover header indicating alternative regions if available.
detailed_policies: Timeouts: Client socket timeout = 8s default, connect timeout = 500ms. Servers respect X-Client-Deadline when provided; runtime enforces per-request server timeout and cancels background work beyond server deadline.
Backoff: Exponential backoff formula t = base * (2^attempt) with full jitter. Base=100ms, max_backoff=3s, attempts=2 (client retries). Total retry budget per logical request <= 8s.

Idempotency key semantics: Header: Idempotency-Key: <UUIDv4>. Tokens are opaque to runtime and used to dedupe side-effects. Server returns Idempotency-Status header with values {replayed, accepted, conflict}. Dedup window default 24h; configurable per-customer. Keys MUST be unique per logical user operation (do not reuse across distinct operations).

Hedging: Condition for hedged duplicate: request latency > route-configured p95_latency_threshold OR explicit client flag hedged=true. Hedged attempts launched after a hedging_delay = max(50ms, p95_latency_threshold * 0.5). Limit 1 hedged attempt per original request. Hedged attempts are counted separately in metrics and can be rate-limited by runtime feature flags.

Circuit breakers: Per-route and per-tenant breakers. Open threshold: 5xx_ratio > 5% in 1m window AND error_count > 100. Half-open probation: allow 5 requests every 10s. Breaker state exposed through admin API and dashboards.

Load shedding: Runtime drops requests by priority. Default priority: auth > inference > background. When overloaded, return 429 with Retry-After. Provide lightweight rejection path for unauthenticated/anonymous workloads to protect authenticated premium traffic.

Telemetry: Clients MUST emit retry metadata (attempt number, reason, idempotency key) as headers for runtime consumption and observability. Runtime records dedupe hits, idempotency conflicts, hedged wins/losses, and aggregated cost impact.

Backward compatibility: If server responds with 501 or header Idempotency-Supported: false, SDKs MUST disable retry for non-idempotent endpoints and surface a clear warning in logs. Old SDKs without the new behavior are subject to increased request failures; we will provide a compatibility library shim for users on unsupported SDK versions.
sdk_compatibility_matrix: Python SDK v3.1+: full support for idempotency header, default retry policy, and hedging opt-in flag
JS SDK v2.8+: supports idempotency and retry flags; browser build will disable hedging by default due to concurrency constraints
Go SDK v1.6+: lightweight header-only implementation; hedging is opt-in and behind runtime feature flag
Other clients: fallback behavior documented; server will return explicit headers when features are not supported and SDKs should respect them
rollout_plan: Week 1: Publish spec and compatibility matrix; SDK owners to open PRs with feature-flagged changes
Week 2: Runtime feature gated rollout to canary region; enable idempotency token storage using Redis cluster (replicated) for canary tenants
Week 3: Canaries with 10% production traffic for selected internal customers; monitor dedupe hit rate and P95/P99 latency
Week 4: Expand to 50% after SLO verification; update public docs and migration guide
Week 5: 100% rollout and deprecation notice for legacy retry behavior in 90 days
testing_plan: Unit tests for SDKs to validate header wiring, backoff timing, and retry counters
Integration tests: staged failure injection to verify dedupe semantics and hedged request winners/losses
Chaos tests: region-level partition to confirm multi-region failover and that coordinated backoffs avoid cascading overload
Load tests: ensure circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shedding behavior preserve high-priority traffic under stress
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Clients may accidentally reuse Idempotency-Keys causing unintended dedupe. Mitigation: document best practices, SDKs auto-generate UUIDs unless caller supplies one, and add a warning when reused frequently.

Risk: Hedging amplifies load during partial outages. Mitigation: hedging is opt-in per route with a global rate limiter and conservative defaults; monitor hedged amplification ratio and disable if >1.2x amplification.
Risk: Increased state/storage for idempotency dedupe. Mitigation: configurable TTLs per customer, efficient Redis schema, and optional spillover to blobstore for long-term entries.
Risk: Backwards compatibility break with older SDKs. Mitigation: compatibility matrix + shim library + clear deprecation timeline and telemetry to detect old SDK usage.
